question: A 50-year-old man comes to the physician because of gradually worsening rhythmic movements of his right hand for the past 5 months. His symptoms worsen when he is in a meeting and he is concerned that people are noticing it more frequently. There is no personal or family history of serious illness, but the patient recalls that his father developed bobbing of the head in older age. He takes no medications. Neurological examination shows a tremor of the right hand when the limbs are relaxed. When the patient is asked to move his arm the tremor decreases. He has reduced arm swing while walking. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "50-year-old man with right hand tremor" -> "tremor worsens with stress" -> "suggestive of essential tremor" -> "essential tremor often treated with beta-blockers" -> "Propranolol is a common first-line treatment" -> 85%

CHAIN: "50-year-old man with right hand tremor" -> "tremor decreases with movement" -> "indicates a possible Parkinsonian feature" -> "Parkinson's disease often treated with Levodopa/carbidopa" -> "but essential tremor is more likely here" -> "Propranolol is appropriate for essential tremor" -> 80%

CHAIN: "50-year-old man with right hand tremor" -> "family history of head bobbing" -> "possible hereditary movement disorder" -> "tremor characteristics suggest essential tremor" -> "Propranolol is effective for essential tremor" -> 90%

CHAIN: "50-year-old man with right hand tremor" -> "neurological exam shows resting tremor" -> "resting tremor is characteristic of Parkinson's disease" -> "Levodopa/carbidopa is a common treatment" -> "but the presentation is more consistent with essential tremor" -> "Propranolol is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's symptoms are suggestive of Parkinson's disease, characterized by a resting tremor, bradykinesia (reduced arm swing), and the fact that the tremor decreases with movement. Given the age of onset and family history of similar symptoms, Levodopa/carbidopa is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for managing Parkinson's disease symptoms.
